materials.title: MATH 235 Syllabus
pages: MATH 235: Introduction to Linear Algebra, Fall 2026. Topics: systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, vector spaces, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, orthogonality.
Grading: written homework 15%, weekly Canvas quizzes 10%, Exam 1 20%, Exam 2 20%, final exam 35%. The lowest quiz score is dropped.
Exams are closed book; a basic scientific calculator is allowed but not a graphing calculator.

materials.title: Notes 5.1-5.2: Eigenvalues
pages: An eigenvector of a square matrix A is a nonzero vector x with Ax = lambda x for some scalar lambda, called the eigenvalue.
lambda is an eigenvalue of A exactly when A - lambda I is not invertible, that is when det(A - lambda I) = 0. This is the characteristic equation.
For a triangular matrix the eigenvalues are the entries on the main diagonal.
To find eigenvectors for an eigenvalue lambda, solve the homogeneous system (A - lambda I)x = 0. The solution set is the eigenspace.
Eigenvectors that belong to distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent.

materials.title: Notes 3.1-3.3: Determinants
pages: The determinant of a 2x2 matrix [a b; c d] is ad - bc. A matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero.
Cofactor expansion works along any row or column, with signs alternating in a checkerboard pattern starting with + in the top-left corner.
Row operations: swapping two rows flips the sign, scaling a row by k scales the determinant by k, adding a multiple of one row to another leaves it unchanged.
det(AB) = det(A) det(B) and det(A transpose) = det(A).
